The three exports use the same reference areas: **1,175.8 m² net floor area** and **1,469.75 m² gross floor area**, tool version **1.13.1_dev**. The reference already includes PV. Variants differ in exported flexibility settings, not a general “without/with PV” comparison.

| Export | Tool preselection | PV flexibility active | Signal-controlled flexibility active |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Bsp_San_6G` | No flexibility | No | No |
| `Bsp_San_6G_pv` | PV only | Yes | No |
| `Bsp_San_6G_flex` | PV + signal | No | Yes |

Preselection labels and actually exported switches are shown separately. Saved inputs and results determine interpretation. [Differing IN values as CSV](../assets/results/input_differences.csv).

## Heat balance {#waermebilanz}

Transmission and ventilation losses, night ventilation and cooling demand are compared with solar/internal gains and heating demand. Contributions are annual energy per net floor area. All three heat balances close within numerical precision.

## Final-energy balance {#endenergiebilanz}

All three variants are entirely electrically supplied; exported district-heating, natural-gas, biomass and other-carrier contributions are zero. The chart shows **electrical final energy for local use**, including building services, user electricity, storage charging and district EV charging.

Direct/flexible PV use, conventional/signal-controlled imports and available discharge flows provide supply. Feed-in and external EV charging are outside this local-use balance. This prevents counting them as local demand coverage; all three balances close.

## Primary-energy balance {#primaerenergiebilanz}

Assessment includes demand, substitution equivalents and context factors. The difference between supply and demand sides is an **assessment result**, not an error in a physically closed balance. Flexibility and context contributions are not additional physical generation.

## GHG balance {#thg-bilanz}

The figure covers exported life-cycle contributions for **2025–2075**: construction, building services and vehicles (EE), and building operation and mobility (OE). Negative contributions, notably feed-in and mobility-boundary effects, retain their signs. The diamond marks the exported total, equal to the sum of displayed components.

The reference is **gross**, not net, floor area. GWP100 describes climate-impact assessment and is distinct from the 50-year study period. L1–L3 reference bands do not replace verification. PV LCA can be modelled but is excluded by the klimaaktiv method and is zero in these exports.

The analysis uses saved exports; no Excel simulation is rerun. Figures record source file, scenario, version and source checksum. They do not establish confirmed declaration status.

[Time-resolved electrical flows](#aspern-f7) are shown separately for **Aspern F7**. Completeness of hourly exports for the three refurbishment variants is being checked for a future extension.

## Aspern F7: time-resolved electrical flows {#aspern-f7}

`Aspern PVCheck _ F7.xlsx` contains 8,760 hourly values on the 2018 timeline. Charts show conventional imports, direct PV use, flexible PV use where nonzero, and PV feed-in. Imports include conventional components grouped under `E_grid` in the schema.

**Boundary:** These are selected flow profiles, not a closed consumption balance. Consumption, storage and complete signal-controlled import channels are absent from this export. Missing quantities are not treated as zero.

### Seasonal mean daily profiles

The four seasons derive from exported calendar information. Each hour of day shows the average over all corresponding hours in the season. Values are mean power in W/m² net floor area, calculated from hourly Wh/m² after verifying a one-hour interval. Seasonal means are not actual daily profiles.

### Chronological hourly values

January and July weeks are directly selectable windows. Zoom, range selection and legend controls support analysis of individual contributions. These weeks provide orientation; they are not statistically representative samples. Positive values represent local PV use and conventional imports, negative values PV feed-in.
